title: Property taxes
prompt: What should Iowa do about property taxes?
context: SF 2472 caps most city and county levy growth at 2% and creates a homestead exemption of 10% of a home's value, with a $5,500 minimum and $20,000 maximum.

options.label: Reduce further
options.description: Reduce property taxes further, even if this requires reductions in some local spending.

options.label: Relief with services protected
options.description: Prioritize tax relief while preserving funding for essential local services.

options.label: Wait and evaluate
options.description: Maintain the current reforms until their effects can be evaluated.

options.label: More local flexibility
options.description: Give local governments more flexibility to fund services.

unansweredQuestions: Neither candidate addressed the levy cap rate, its exceptions, the EMS levy, or the state backfill.

title: State income taxes and government spending
prompt: What should Iowa do with the state income tax?
context: Iowa's income tax is a flat 3.8%. The State Auditor has warned of a projected budget gap after recent cuts.

options.label: Phase it out
options.description: Phase the income tax out over time, paid for by reducing state spending.

options.label: Keep the current rate
options.description: Keep the current 3.8% flat rate.

options.label: Pause further cuts
options.description: Make no further cuts until the state budget is balanced.

options.label: Raise rates on higher incomes
options.description: Raise rates on higher incomes to address the budget gap.

unansweredQuestions: SJR 11: no documented position for either candidate.
Neither candidate has a plan for the FY2027 budget gap.

title: Cost of living and housing affordability
prompt: Which approach should Iowa prioritize to make housing more affordable?
context: Proposals from both candidates focus on housing supply, investor purchases, and help for first-time buyers.

options.label: Allow more housing types
options.description: Loosen zoning and permitting rules so more kinds of housing, such as duplexes and accessory units, can be built.

options.label: Limit investor purchases
options.description: Restrict large investors and hedge funds from buying single-family homes.

options.label: Help first-time buyers
options.description: Help first-time buyers with down payment assistance.

options.label: Leave it to the market
options.description: Leave housing mainly to the private market, with few new state programs.

title: Farm profitability and agricultural policy
prompt: What should the state do first to improve farm profitability?
context: Farm income is shaped by input costs, land prices, trade, and who owns farmland.

options.label: Challenge input monopolies
options.description: Use state antitrust enforcement against large agricultural input companies.

options.label: Limit outside land ownership
options.description: Limit outside investors and corporations from buying farmland.

options.label: Push for open trade
options.description: Press federal officials to reduce tariffs and expand export markets.

options.label: Keep the state's role limited
options.description: Keep state involvement limited and let markets set farm economics.

unansweredQuestions: Neither candidate named Iowa Code ch. 9H or 10B, or explained how land confiscation or antitrust suits would work legally.

title: Eminent domain and landowner protections
prompt: Should Iowa restrict eminent domain when the main beneficiary is a private company?
context: Eminent domain lets the government take private property for public use with compensation. Its use for privately owned projects, such as CO2 pipelines, has been debated in Iowa.
learnMore: Supporting a general principle is different from supporting a specific bill. Both candidates have stated the general principle; neither committed to signing HF 2104.

options.label: Prohibit it for private benefit
options.description: Prohibit eminent domain when the main beneficiary is a private company.

options.label: Stricter standards
options.description: Allow it only under stricter standards, with stronger landowner compensation.

options.label: Case by case
options.description: Keep current law and let regulators decide case by case.

unansweredQuestions: Neither candidate said whether he would sign HF 2104.
Neither addressed the Utilities Commission, Summit's permit, or IUC appointment criteria.

title: Drinking water, nitrates, and environmental regulation
prompt: What should be Iowa's main approach to reducing nitrates in drinking water?
context: Nitrate runoff from farmland affects drinking water in parts of Iowa. Current policy relies mostly on voluntary conservation practices.

options.label: Expand farmer incentives
options.description: Expand incentives and tax credits for farmers who adopt conservation practices.

options.label: Enforceable limits
options.description: Set enforceable limits on farm nutrient runoff.

options.label: Monitoring and alerts first
options.description: Focus first on expanding water monitoring and public alerts.

options.label: Keep the current approach
options.description: Keep the current voluntary approach without major changes.

unansweredQuestions: Neither candidate addressed HF 2771 water treatment funding or Iowa Flood Center funding.

title: Cancer prevention and public health
prompt: What should be Iowa's main approach to its high cancer rates?
context: Both candidates rank cancer as a top priority and both oppose legal immunity for pesticide makers.

options.label: Research and coordination
options.description: Fund more cancer research and a coordinated state task force.

options.label: Test environmental exposures
options.description: Investigate and test environmental exposures such as farm chemicals and consumer products.

options.label: Prevention and screening
options.description: Focus on prevention, such as tobacco taxes, screening, and radon awareness.

options.label: Existing programs
options.description: Rely mainly on existing federal and university programs.

title: Rural hospitals and health care access
prompt: How should Iowa support rural hospitals and access to care?
context: Rural hospitals depend heavily on Medicaid and Medicare payments.

options.label: Raise reimbursement rates
options.description: Raise Medicaid reimbursement rates paid to providers.

options.label: Faster payment
options.description: Require insurers to pay providers promptly and simplify billing.

options.label: Regional care centers
options.description: Support consolidation into regional care centers rather than keeping every facility.

options.label: Fewer regulations
options.description: Reduce regulations and let providers compete.

unansweredQuestions: HF 2635: no documented position for either candidate.

title: Medicaid and health coverage
prompt: How should Iowa run its Medicaid program?
context: Iowa Medicaid is administered by private managed care companies. A federal work requirement is scheduled to begin December 1, 2026.

options.label: Return to state administration
options.description: End privately managed Medicaid and return to state administration.

options.label: Keep it, with more oversight
options.description: Keep private managed care, with stronger oversight of the companies.

options.label: Keep it as it is
options.description: Keep the current system mostly as it is.

unansweredQuestions: Neither candidate addressed the December 1 work requirement start date, its exceptions, or verification.

title: Public school funding
prompt: How should Iowa fund its public schools?
context: The legislature sets the annual increase in per-pupil state aid to school districts.

options.label: Increase significantly
options.description: Increase state aid significantly, above recent annual increases.

options.label: Modest increases
options.description: Continue modest annual increases similar to recent years.

options.label: Hold steady
options.description: Hold funding steady and focus on efficiency and flexibility.

title: Private school tuition assistance and school choice
prompt: What should Iowa do with Education Savings Accounts (state-funded private school tuition)?
context: Iowa's ESA program is open to all families. The State Auditor's report put the FY2026 program cost at $329.6 million; other published figures conflict.
learnMore: ESA cost figures conflict: the framework gives $8,148 per student for 2026-27; Iowa Starting Line reported $5,400 per student (unverified).

options.label: Keep universal and expand
options.description: Keep ESAs open to all families and expand the program.

options.label: Keep as is
options.description: Keep the universal program without major changes.

options.label: Add income limits
options.description: Keep ESAs but limit eligibility by family income.

options.label: Phase out
options.description: Phase out ESAs and return the funds to public schools.

title: Parental rights and education policy
prompt: Should Iowa require vaccinations for school enrollment?
context: Iowa requires certain vaccinations for school enrollment, with exemptions.

options.label: Keep current requirements
options.description: Keep current school vaccine requirements and exemptions.

options.label: Easier exemptions
options.description: Keep requirements but make exemptions easier for parents to obtain.

options.label: End requirements
options.description: End vaccine requirements for school enrollment.

unansweredQuestions: HPV consent law: no documented position for either candidate.

title: Abortion law and reproductive protections
prompt: What should Iowa's abortion law be?
context: Iowa law limits abortion after about six weeks of pregnancy, with exceptions.

options.label: Restrict further
options.description: Restrict abortion further than current law.

options.label: Keep current law
options.description: Keep the current six-week law.

options.label: Broaden access
options.description: Restore broader access, similar to the Roe v. Wade framework.

unansweredQuestions: Lahn's position on exceptions for rape, incest, or the life of the mother is not verified.

title: Firearm rights and public safety
prompt: What should Iowa's approach to firearm laws be?
context: Iowa's constitution protects the right to keep and bear arms (Art. I §1A).

options.label: Expand gun rights
options.description: Further reduce restrictions on owning and carrying firearms.

options.label: Keep current law
options.description: Keep current firearm laws as they are.

options.label: Add safety measures
options.description: Add new safety measures, such as permit or red-flag requirements.

unansweredQuestions: The research does not establish a verified current firearms position for either candidate.

title: Religious freedom and civil rights
prompt: Should the Iowa Civil Rights Act protect people from discrimination based on gender identity?
context: SF 418 removed gender identity as a protected class from the Iowa Civil Rights Act.

options.label: Restore protection
options.description: Restore gender identity as a protected class in the Iowa Civil Rights Act.

options.label: Keep the current law
options.description: Keep the law as amended by SF 418.

unansweredQuestions: SF 579 and facilities: no documented position for either candidate.

title: Immigration enforcement
prompt: What role should state government play in immigration?
context: Immigration status is set by federal law; states control their own benefits, hiring, and cooperation with federal agencies.

options.label: Require cooperation
options.description: Require state and local police to cooperate with federal immigration enforcement.

options.label: Bar state benefits
options.description: Bar people in the country illegally from state benefits.

options.label: Leave it to the federal government
options.description: Leave immigration enforcement to the federal government.

options.label: Focus on law-abiding workers
options.description: Focus on making law-abiding immigrant workers feel safe in Iowa.

unansweredQuestions: ICE cooperation, 287(g), E-Verify, SF 2340, and SF 2218: no documented position for either candidate.

title: Energy, data centers, and utility costs
prompt: How should Iowa handle large data centers?
context: Data centers use large amounts of electricity and water and have received state tax incentives.

options.label: No breaks; pay their own costs
options.description: End tax breaks and require data centers to cover their own utility and infrastructure costs.

options.label: Pause new construction
options.description: Pause new data center construction statewide.

options.label: Let counties decide
options.description: Let each county decide whether and how to allow data centers.

options.label: Keep incentives
options.description: Keep offering incentives to attract data centers for jobs and tax base.

title: Jobs, wages, and workforce development
prompt: What should Iowa do about the state minimum wage, currently $7.25 an hour?
context: Iowa's minimum wage matches the federal minimum of $7.25 an hour.

options.label: Raise and index
options.description: Raise it in phases, for example to $12, and then adjust it automatically for inflation.

options.label: Raise modestly
options.description: Raise it modestly, without automatic adjustments.

options.label: Keep at $7.25
options.description: Keep it at the federal minimum of $7.25.

options.label: Local option
options.description: Let cities and counties set their own minimum wages.

title: Government transparency and accountability
prompt: How should Iowa strengthen oversight of state government?
context: A 2023 law limited the State Auditor's access to some records.

options.label: Restore auditor access
options.description: Restore the State Auditor's full access to records by reversing the 2023 limits.

options.label: Independent audits
options.description: Rely more on independent third-party audits of state programs.

options.label: Current oversight is enough
options.description: Keep current oversight; it is sufficient.

title: Elections, individual privacy, and state government authority
prompt: Should more decisions be made by counties and cities rather than the state?
context: The legislature decides which powers counties and cities hold. Related issues include voting methods, privacy, and executive power.

options.label: More local control
options.description: Give counties and cities more control over local decisions.

options.label: Keep the current balance
options.description: Keep the current balance between state and local authority.

options.label: More uniform state rules
options.description: Set more uniform statewide rules.

unansweredQuestions: Voter ID and early voting: no documented position for either candidate.
